newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Soquimich starts lithium output.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Soquimich starts lithium output.

text.p: Chile's Sociedad Quimica y Minera de Chile SA (Soquimich) has started producing lithium at its Minsal salt lake mine in northern Chile, said the project's general manager Felipe Anguita.
"Startup began on October 1...and we reached full capacity at the start of the month," Anguita told Reuters in a telephone interview.
The company, Chile's largest fertilizer producer, shipped its first exports of 150 tonnes of lithium from the northern port of Antofagasta to Europe Monday, he said.
The mine should produce 700 tonnes of lithium carbonate this year with output rising to 12,000 tonnes next year, he said.
Aguita said the world lithium market has already reacted to Minsal's production with prices falling from $1.30-$1.50 a pound at the start of November to around $1 in mid-Decmember.
""We're starting to see changes in the market...prices are starting to go down," said Anguita.

Soquimich has launched an agressive campaign to sell lithium from Minsal and break the dominance of the world's two largest lithium producers FMC Corp and Cyprus Foote Mineral, part of Cyprus Amax Minerals Co.
The minsal plant, which cost $50 million to build, has an installed production capacity of 40 million pounds -- equivalent to a around third of the world's lithium output.
